newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria, Yugoslavia to agree investment protection.
newsitem.headline: Austria, Yugoslavia to agree investment protection.

text.p: Austria and Yugoslavia said on Thursday they expected to sign an agreement on investment protection in the next few days, opening the door for closer ties after the lifting of U.N. sanctions against Belgrade.

Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel told reporters a meeting with Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic in Vienna had been "a very positive development" for relations between the two countries.
"We expect an agreement within the next few days," said Schuessel. "It's an important agreement, as much in our interest as theirs."
Milutinovic's visit was the first by a Yugoslav cabinet minister to Vienna since the former Yugoslav federation disintegrated in 1991.
Milutinovic said he welcomed the resumption of ties.
"We had tremendous economic relations before five years ago and we consider Austria one of our most important economic partners," he said.
Austria hoped to bring trade to its former level, which at its peak in 1990 saw an exchange of goods amounting to more than 2.5 billion schillings ($240 million), Schuessel said.
"We see an enormous recovery during the first quarter of 1996, up to 300 million schillings," he added.

The Security Council formally ended all trade sanctions against Yugoslavia, which now comprises only the republics of Serbia and Montenegro. The sanctions were imposed in 1992 for the republics' role in stoking war in neighbouring Bosnia.
Schuessel and Milutinovic said a new agreement on social security for Yugoslav citizens living in Austria and the repatriation of convicted Yugoslavs or immigrants was also imminent.
The two ministers touched on the subject of human rights, and Schuessel said the stability of the region depended on the correct treatment of minorities. ($1=10.72 Schilling)
